working_title: County Down's Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Playing Royal County Down, Ardglass and Kirkistown Castle
angle: County Down is one of the world's great golf destinations, anchored by Royal County Down at the top of every global ranking, but most visitors fly in, play one round and leave. This guide makes the case for spending three or four days touring the full circuit, including the more accessible (and dramatically cheaper) courses at Ardglass and Kirkistown Castle, with practical logistics for UK visitors travelling by air or ferry.
research_notes:
- Royal County Down (RCD), Newcastle, Co. Down: opened 1889, designed with input from Old Tom Morris, Harry Vardon and Harry Colt; ranked No.1 in the world by Golf Digest for 2024; par-71 Championship Links plus a secondary 18-hole Annesley Links (par-67). Backdrop: Mourne Mountains and Dundrum Bay.
- RCD visitor days (Championship): Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday, Sunday (afternoons only on Sunday). No visitor play Wednesday or Saturday. No online booking portal; all bookings by phone or email only. Tee sheet for each season typically released in spring; peak summer slots (June–August Mon/Thu mornings) reportedly sell out within hours of opening.
- RCD 2026 green fees: £450 per player on the Championship Links; £120 on the Annesley Links. Full prepayment required; non-refundable. Caddie hire available (prices vary; confirm with club). No ATM on site.
- Getting to County Down from mainland UK: Belfast has two airports (George Best Belfast City Airport, approx. 30–40 min drive to Newcastle; Belfast International, approx. 1 hr 15 min). Ferry options: Stena Line Cairnryan–Belfast (~2 hrs 15 min); P&O Ferries Cairnryan–Larne (~2 hrs); Stena Line Liverpool Birkenhead–Belfast (~8 hrs, overnight available). Newcastle is approx. 45 min from Belfast via A24. A hire car is strongly recommended for the circuit.
- Ardglass Golf Club: 18-hole clifftop links, Castle Place, Ardglass, BT30 7TP. Founded 1896; par-70; 6,216 yards. Visitors welcome. Approx. 30 min drive from Royal County Down at Newcastle. Clubhouse incorporates a 15th-century castle structure. Open to visitors; advance booking advised.
- Ardglass green fees: indicative visitor rate around £115 weekday / £135 weekend in high season (sources vary; confirm directly with club). Significantly more affordable than RCD.
- Kirkistown Castle Golf Club: 18-hole links, 142 Main Road, Cloughey, Ards Peninsula, BT22 1JA. Founded 1902; layout attributed to James Braid (1934); par-69; 6,167 yards. Most easterly 18-hole course on the island of Ireland. Approx. 45 min from Belfast. Open to visitors 7 days a week; advance booking essential. Quick-draining sandy links; rarely closed in winter.
- Kirkistown signature hole: par-4 10th ('Long Reach'), 435 yards, elevated plateau green, regarded as one of the hardest par-4s in Irish golf. First and 18th holes share a fairway. WWII airfield construction left a distinctive feature near the first tee known as 'The Dip'.
- Kirkistown green fees: indicative £35 midweek / £40 weekend (sources vary slightly; check directly with club). Historically named Best Value Golf Experience in Ulster.
- Kilkeel Golf Club: parkland course at Mourne Park, Kilkeel, BT34 4LB; 18 holes, par-72, 6,615 yards; set within the Kilmorey Estate at the foot of the Mourne Mountains. Mature woodland and rhododendron; hosted 1999 British Amateur co-hosted with RCD. Rack rate approx. £35–£50 depending on day and source; confirm directly. Good option to include on a multi-day itinerary as a parkland contrast.
- Suggested circuit base: Newcastle (Slieve Donard Resort nearby, or smaller Burrendale Hotel approx. 1 mile from RCD gates). Belfast also viable as a hub with ~45 min drive to RCD.
- Practical notes: wind is a constant factor at all coastal/links courses; a full waterproof suit essential. Mourne mist descends quickly. Handicap certificate required at RCD (and advisable to carry for all). No ATM at RCD; bring cash for caddies.
